searchText: I threw together a precompile based approach to sponsored transactions over here: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3074 Anyone know why the anydot folks stopped pursuing their opcode based approach? I sent this to Patrick McCorry, he sent back: We think its still a good solution, but for any.sender we no longer relay meta-transactions via an intermediary relay contract. We just send it directly to the target contract. We realized if we want to support rollups, then we have to avoid .call() as the gas costs are quadratic for the calldata passed through it. Quadratic? Pretty sure it is linear with number of frames you have to pass the calldata through. his response: so when you do a .call(), the memory allocation is quadratic. so for rollups, we were told for a full block the overhead of the .call() can be up to 30% of the gas cost since so much calldata is being sent through the .call()
